query: Consider the following context: Materials capable of withstanding extreme environments open promising opportunities for nuclear fusion reactors. In that context, which material can be used for interlayer materials between W and CuCrZr, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Tungsten carbide (WC) can be used as an interlayer material between W and CuCrZr for nuclear fusion reactors.
generation.material_initial_state: Tungsten (W) and CuCrZr in their pure forms
generation.intervention: Introduction of tungsten carbide (WC) as an interlayer material
generation.conditions: Extreme environments, such as high temperatures and radiation
generation.mechanism: WC acts as a diffusion barrier, reducing the reaction between W and CuCrZr
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved thermal and mechanical stability of the W-CuCrZr interface
generation.baseline: W and CuCrZr without an interlayer material
generation.uncertainty: High, due to lack of specific data on the performance of WC as an interlayer material in extreme environments

falsification_experiment.design: Comparative study of W-CuCrZr interfaces with and without WC interlayer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the W-CuCrZr interface with WC interlayer shows no significant improvement in thermal and mechanical stability compared to the interface without WC, the hypothesis is falsified
